## M1 · BENCH-parallel-verdicts — May cases run in parallel on one host count as a merge-gate verdict, and under what rule?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 11

Evidence: Rule written on docs/testbench.md 'On a shared host' and committed on main as 7760bb18d (docs-only; cargo testbench docs PASS, git diff --check clean; three editor rounds, the last BLOCK's class gap closed with the editor's own wording). Scheduler follows it: .wash/local/jobs.mk runs host-tests, ssh-loopback and [net] cases via `jobserver all` (alone), boot cases shared. MEM1's gate applies it first: its 56 host-clock cases rerun alone.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `1f8cd43582ef358253fee8ce6ce8e462` · 2026-10-05T22:02:30Z

> Owner's direction tonight (2026-10-05): use the 24-core host; the orchestrator built a make-based scheduler (.wash/local/jobs.mk over a machine-wide GNU make fifo jobserver, .wash/local/jobserver: 24 tokens shared by every make target and every rustc under them; a case holds one extra token for its guest). So several DIFFERENT cases, or different packages' runs, now run side by side, each with its own run dir (B7), total runnable work bounded by the token count, no cpuset pinning. docs/testbench.md (The seed sweep, ~187-192) says a result under `--jobs` above 1 is a sweep datum, not a verdict, and that the whole bench runs serially for that reason; the stated hazards were guest timing under load and port races for [net] cases. Question: (1) does that rule extend to different cases run concurrently under a bounded token pool, or is it specific to parallel seeds of one case; (2) if parallel results may be verdicts, what is the rule: e.g. 'a timing case (sched-*, latency targets, 20 s bounds) that fails under sharing is rerun alone, and the gate line records which cases ran shared'; or 'timing cases always run alone, the rest may share'; (3) where it is written (testbench.md's sweep paragraph, or a new short 'Running the bench on a shared host' paragraph). Evidence so far: AIO1's timeout-based client tests flaked three times under load (ASID1's bench 2026-10-03, VOL1's host run and MEM1's bench tonight at load 11-18, oversubscribed) and passed alone each time; no guest timing case has yet been seen to flake under the token pool (it is new). Not blocking: tonight's final gates still run as serial `cargo testbench` on the final head; this decides the rule for tomorrow.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `741b906dcbfc473ce19f5f9db2d1b940` · 2026-10-05T22:04:23Z

> (1) The sweep rule's reason was never "seeds of one case": it was the clock. It neither extends wholesale to concurrent cases nor exempts them; it splits by what the case measures with.
> 
> (2) The rule, now written: a guest case measures in guest time (icount, pinned seed: the run repeats exactly under any load), so its pass, and a failure the guest itself reports, are verdicts wherever it ran, beside whatever. Its one host-clock exposure is timeout_secs (qemu.rs:529, a wall deadline); a case that only ran out of it beside other work has no verdict and is rerun alone. A case that measures with the host's clock has a verdict only run alone, no other bench work and no build beside it: every host-tests case (build.rs:318 runs cargo test with a thread per core outside any job bound; libs/client aio/console, libs/rt mux/sleep/parked_write/given_up, keyd timing, consoled assert wall-clock bounds) and every [net] case (host sockets in wall time; the port race). A merge's whole bench may run its guest cases side by side under one bounded pool and must run its host-clock cases after them one at a time; the report names the cases that ran shared. No tolerance on the timing tests: three flakes under oversubscription, each passing alone, is evidence for "alone", not for a wider bound.
> 
> So the make scheduler is right for guest cases (one token per guest) and must give host-tests and [net] targets exclusivity: a serial tail after all guest targets, no build running. That is where AIO1's flakes came from, not the token pool.
> 
> (3) Written on docs/testbench.md: the sweep paragraph points at a new "On a shared host" paragraph below it (the old serial-merge and [net] wording folded in). Edited in the root working tree, uncommitted: commit it as a docs commit before the next merge touches testbench.md, or tell me to move the text under .wash/local.
> 
> Not an owner choice: nothing weakens; it states what was always true of icount.
